title: Iterated Ball Nonacceptance
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a state of the counting procedure. Set $K=2^{2E\sigma.lg+2E\sigma.s}$, and form the balls using the relation and initial predicate determined by $\mathrm{orc}$, $x$, and $\sigma.s$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, its exponent register is zero, its designated scratch registers are clear, $K+1\le B$, and the ball of radius zero has cardinality one. Suppose that for every $k',T',v',c'\le B$, the counting procedure at its comparison stage, with exponent zero, code bound and stage index $K$, next stage index $K+1$, those four register values, and the ball of radius $K$'s cardinality in its known-ball-size register, terminates and has accepting computation exactly when $Q$ holds. Then the procedure started at $\sigma$ in the false-phase round state with $E$ rounds remaining terminates, and has an accepting computation exactly when both $Q$ holds and no vertex in any ball of radius $j$, for $0<j\le K$, is accepting.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle from four indices and Boolean words to Boolean answers
Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
Ball of radius zero has cardinality one
For all $k',T',v',c'\le B$, the specified comparison-stage computation has semantic property $Q$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be an
oracle, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a
machine state. Write $K=2^{2E\sigma.\mathrm{lg}+2E\sigma.s}$, and form the balls using
the relation and initial predicate determined by $\mathrm{orc}$, $x$, and $\sigma.s$.
Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, its exponent register $e$ is zero,
its designated scratch registers are clear, $K+1\le B$, and the ball at radius zero has
cardinality one. Suppose also that for every $k',T',v',c'\le B$, the machine started at
the comparison stage with $e=0$, $K$ as its code bound, $k',T',v',c'$ in the
corresponding registers, stage index $K$, next stage index $K+1$, and the cardinality of
the ball at radius $K$ in the count register, has semantic property $Q$. Then the
machine started at round $E$ with the false phase and state $\sigma$ has the semantic
property that no vertex in any ball of radius $j$ is accepting for every $0<j\le K$, and
that $Q$ holds.
